figures.alt: Compact framed under-stairs half-bath rough-in with toilet drain stub, supply lines, vent connection, and sloped stair underside
figures.caption: A bathroom addition is a new room with structural, plumbing, electrical, ventilation, accessibility, and finish requirements. The available space must work as a complete assembly.

figures.alt: Vanity cabinet with accessible sink P-trap, supply valves, and service clearance
figures.caption: Drain routing and service access are practical design constraints. The location of the new bath affects slab or framing work, venting, supply lines, slope, and the future ability to maintain the room.
figures.before: Where the Drain Goes: The Hardest Part of a Bathroom Addition

figures.alt: Master bath shower at waterproofing stage with sloped pan, curb, membrane, drain, wall framing, and plumbing rough-in
figures.caption: The sequence matters: layout, rough-in, inspection, waterproofing, finishes, fixtures, and final testing need to occur in the right order before the bathroom is ready for use.
figures.before: The Construction Sequence for a Bathroom Addition
